title: The connecting maps of right derived functors computed from horseshoe resolutions are well defined and natural
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category with enough injectives, $\mathcal B$ an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a left exact additive functor and $R^nv$ ($n\ge0$) its right derived functors computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive], [def-sp-injective-resolutions], with the isomorphisms $\iota^n_P:R^nv(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^n(v(P^\bullet))$ for injective resolutions $s:X\to P^\bullet$ with $P^q=0$ for $q<0$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. For a short exact sequence $S:0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$ of $\mathcal A$, a *horseshoe resolution* of $S$ is a datum $H=(s_A,s_B,s_C,\alpha,\beta)$ of injective resolutions $s_A:A\to I_A^\bullet$, $s_B:B\to I_B^\bullet$, $s_C:C\to I_C^\bullet$ with $I_A^q=I_B^q=I_C^q=0$ for $q<0$ and morphisms of complexes $\alpha:I_A^\bullet\to I_B^\bullet$, $\beta:I_B^\bullet\to I_C^\bullet$ with $\alpha^0s_A=s_Bf$, $\beta^0s_B=s_Cg$ and $0\to I_A^n\xrightarrow{\alpha^n}I_B^n\xrightarrow{\beta^n}I_C^n\to0$ short exact for every $n$ (horseshoe resolutions exist by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses]). For such $H$ the sequence of complexes $0\to v(I_A^\bullet)\xrightarrow{v(\alpha)}v(I_B^\bullet)\xrightarrow{v(\beta)}v(I_C^\bullet)\to0$ of $\mathcal B$ is short exact in each degree (each $0\to I_A^n\to I_B^n\to I_C^n\to0$ splits because $I_A^n$ is injective, and $v$ is additive); let $\partial^n_H:H^n(v(I_C^\bullet))\to H^{n+1}(v(I_A^\bullet))$ be its connecting morphisms (the snake-lemma connecting morphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]), and put $\delta^n_H:=(\iota^{n+1}_{I_A})^{-1}\circ\partial^n_H\circ\iota^n_{I_C}:R^nv(C)\to R^{n+1}v(A)$. Then: (1) for every morphism $(a,b,c)$ of short exact sequences from $S$ to a short exact sequence $S':0\to A'\xrightarrow{f'}B'\xrightarrow{g'}C'\to0$ (so $bf=f'a$, $cg=g'b$), every horseshoe resolution $H$ of $S$ and every horseshoe resolution $H'$ of $S'$, one has $R^{n+1}v(a)\circ\delta^n_H=\delta^n_{H'}\circ R^nv(c)$ for all $n\ge0$; in particular (taking $S'=S$ and $(a,b,c)$ the identities) $\delta^n_H$ does not depend on $H$, and one writes $\delta^n_S$; (2) the $R^nv$ are additive functors and $(R^nv,\delta_S)_{n\ge0}$ is a $\delta$-functor from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]: for every $S$ the sequence $0\to R^0v(A)\xrightarrow{R^0v(f)}R^0v(B)\xrightarrow{R^0v(g)}R^0v(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^0_S}R^1v(A)\to\cdots\to R^nv(C)\xrightarrow{\delta^n_S}R^{n+1}v(A)\to\cdots$ is exact, and the $\delta_S$ are natural in $S$ by (1). (The $\delta^n_S$ are the connecting maps constructed from a horseshoe resolution for [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact]; no claim is made here about their relation to the connecting maps of the universal right-derived delta-functor construction, which come from distinguished triangles.)

source.place: No Stacks statement (Stacks builds the delta-functor R^*F from triangles, Lemma Tag 05TE); the horseshoe construction is Lemma Tag 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses) with Homology Lemma Tag 0117 (homology.tex, lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain, functorial in the short exact sequence); the classical statement is Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, Theorem 2.4.6 with the horseshoe Lemma 2.2.8 (not in literature/, WANTED). Route suggested by the worker for the split: for H, H' form the degreewise pushout Q_X = coker(X[0] -> I_X (+) I'_X, x |-> (s_X x, -s'_{X'}(x_*(x)))) for X = A, B, C (x_* = a, b, c); by the long exact cohomology sequence Q is a degreewise short exact sequence of resolutions of S' (augmentation through I'), H -> Q lifts (a,b,c) and H' -> Q lifts the identity; apply Lemma 013T (complexes, part (2)) to Q to get a horseshoe K with a map Q -> K; then compare partial_H, partial_K, partial_{H'} by naturality of connecting maps (Homology 0117) and lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift

proof.text: Step 1 (additivity). Use the proved upstream instance in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.RightDerived: the chosen injective-resolution functor is additive (sums of lifts represent the same morphism as a lift of the sum up to homotopy), and its composite with v.mapHomotopyCategory and the homology functor is additive. Consequently each R^n v is additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], using enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and additivity of v [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. No degree-zero comparison with v is needed.

source.place: Section Tag 013G (section-injective-resolutions), Lemma Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift) for the lifts; Lemma Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived) for R^n v computed by injective resolutions

proof.text: **Step 2 (for a horseshoe resolution $H$, $v(H)$ is short exact in each degree, so $\partial_H$ and $\delta_H$ are defined).** Let $H=(s_A,s_B,s_C,\alpha,\beta)$ be a horseshoe resolution of $S$ and fix $n\ge0$. Since $\alpha^n$ is a monomorphism and $I_A^n$ is injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions], the identity of $I_A^n$ extends along $\alpha^n$: there is $r:I_B^n\to I_A^n$ with $r\alpha^n=\mathrm{id}$. The endomorphism $e=\mathrm{id}-\alpha^nr$ of $I_B^n$ satisfies $e\alpha^n=0$; since $\beta^n$ is a cokernel of $\alpha^n$ (exactness of the row), $e=\sigma\beta^n$ for a unique $\sigma:I_C^n\to I_B^n$, and $\beta^n\sigma\beta^n=\beta^ne=\beta^n$ with $\beta^n$ epi gives $\beta^n\sigma=\mathrm{id}$. So $r\alpha^n=\mathrm{id}$, $\beta^n\sigma=\mathrm{id}$, $\beta^n\alpha^n=0$, $\alpha^nr+\sigma\beta^n=\mathrm{id}$. The functor $v$ is additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], so these four identities hold for $v(\alpha^n),v(\beta^n),v(r),v(\sigma)$, and they make $0\to v(I_A^n)\to v(I_B^n)\to v(I_C^n)\to0$ short exact in the abelian category $\mathcal B$ [def-sp-abelian]: $v(\alpha^n)$ is a split mono, $v(\beta^n)$ a split epi, and $\mathrm{id}-v(\alpha^n)v(r)=v(\sigma)v(\beta^n)$ vanishes on $\ker v(\beta^n)$, so $\ker v(\beta^n)=\operatorname{im}v(\alpha^n)$. The termwise images $v(\alpha),v(\beta)$ are morphisms of complexes since $v$ preserves composition. Hence $0\to v(I_A^\bullet)\to v(I_B^\bullet)\to v(I_C^\bullet)\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence of $\mathbf N$-indexed cochain complexes of $\mathcal B$, its connecting morphisms $\partial^n_H$ are defined [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], and so is $\delta^n_H=(\iota^{n+1}_{I_A})^{-1}\partial^n_H\iota^n_{I_C}$. (Only additivity of $v$ is used.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0136 (lemma-characterize-injectives), (1) => (3): a short exact sequence 0 -> I -> A -> B -> 0 with I injective splits; as used in derived.tex Lemma Tag 013T, proof Step 1 ('the lower short exact sequence is termwise split'); Lemma Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain) for the connecting maps

proof.text: **Step 3 (clause (1): naturality for any two horseshoe resolutions).** Let $(a,b,c):S\to S'$, $H=(s_A,s_B,s_C,\alpha,\beta)$ a horseshoe resolution of $S$ and $H'=(s'_{A'},s'_{B'},s'_{C'},\alpha',\beta')$ one of $S'$, with complexes $I_X^\bullet$ and $I'^\bullet_{X'}$. Choose morphisms of complexes $\varphi_A:I_A^\bullet\to I'^\bullet_{A'}$, $\varphi_C:I_C^\bullet\to I'^\bullet_{C'}$ with $\varphi_A^0s_A=s'_{A'}a$, $\varphi_C^0s_C=s'_{C'}c$ [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists]; by [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-morphism-lift] there is a morphism of complexes $\varphi_B:I_B^\bullet\to I'^\bullet_{B'}$ with $\varphi_B\alpha=\alpha'\varphi_A$ and $\beta'\varphi_B=\varphi_C\beta$. Applying the additive functor $v$ termwise [def-sp-left-exact-additive] gives morphisms of complexes $u_X=v(\varphi_X)$ with $v(\alpha')u_A=u_Bv(\alpha)$ and $v(\beta')u_B=u_Cv(\beta)$, i.e. a morphism between the degreewise short exact sequences of Step 2 for $H$ and for $H'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality], $H^{n+1}(u_A)\circ\partial^n_H=\partial^n_{H'}\circ H^n(u_C)$. Since $\varphi_A$ lifts $a$ and $\varphi_C$ lifts $c$, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] gives $R^{n+1}v(a)=(\iota^{n+1}_{I'_{A'}})^{-1}H^{n+1}(u_A)\iota^{n+1}_{I_A}$ and $R^nv(c)=(\iota^n_{I'_{C'}})^{-1}H^n(u_C)\iota^n_{I_C}$. Hence $R^{n+1}v(a)\circ\delta^n_H=(\iota^{n+1}_{I'_{A'}})^{-1}H^{n+1}(u_A)\partial^n_H\iota^n_{I_C}=(\iota^{n+1}_{I'_{A'}})^{-1}\partial^n_{H'}H^n(u_C)\iota^n_{I_C}=(\iota^{n+1}_{I'_{A'}})^{-1}\partial^n_{H'}\iota^n_{I'_{C'}}R^nv(c)=\delta^n_{H'}\circ R^nv(c)$ for all $n\ge0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain): 'The construction produces long exact cohomology sequences which are functorial in the short exact sequence'; with derived.tex Lemma Tag 013P (lemma-morphisms-lift). Classically Weibel, Theorem 2.4.6, proof of naturality (not in literature/, WANTED)

proof.text: **Step 4 (independence of the horseshoe).** Take $S'=S$ and $(a,b,c)=(\mathrm{id}_A,\mathrm{id}_B,\mathrm{id}_C)$ in Step 3. As $R^nv$ and $R^{n+1}v$ are functors [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift], $R^{n+1}v(\mathrm{id}_A)$ and $R^nv(\mathrm{id}_C)$ are identities, so $\delta^n_H=\delta^n_{H'}$ for any two horseshoe resolutions $H,H'$ of $S$; this common value is $\delta^n_S$, and Step 3 reads $R^{n+1}v(a)\circ\delta^n_S=\delta^n_{S'}\circ R^nv(c)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain), functoriality applied to the identity of the short exact sequence

proof.text: Step 5 (exactness, including the initial zero). For any horseshoe H, apply the three Mathlib homology_exact lemmas to v(H) [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. The lift comparison [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] gives R^n v(f) iota_IB = iota_IA H^n(v(alpha)) and R^n v(g) iota_IC = iota_IB H^n(v(beta)); the definition of delta_H gives delta_H iota_IA = iota_IC partial_H. At each of the three positions, these equations define a ShortComplex.isoMk from the derived sequence to the homology sequence. The zero composite in the derived sequence follows by cancelling the last comparison isomorphism; ShortComplex.exact_of_iso gives exactness. In degree zero, v(alpha)^0 is monic because its row is split exact (Step 2). Since no natural-number degree precedes zero, Mathlib's mono_homologyMap_of_mono_of_not_rel makes H^0(v(alpha)) monic. Its conjugate R^0 v(f) is then monic as well. Choose a horseshoe using [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses] and use its boundary for the delta-functor; Step 4 compares it to every other horseshoe.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain), for complexes vanishing in negative degrees; derived.tex Lemma Tag 013T (lemma-injective-resolution-ses), parts (2)-(3), for the existence of the horseshoe; derived.tex Lemma Tag 015B (lemma-higher-derived-functors) part (1) is the statement Stacks proves by triangles instead

proof.text: **Step 6 ($\delta$-functor).** By Step 1 the $R^nv$ are additive functors, by Step 5 the sequence of axiom (1) is exact for every short exact sequence, and by Steps 3-4 the $\delta_S$ satisfy axiom (2); so $(R^nv,\delta_S)_{n\ge0}$ is a $\delta$-functor from $\mathcal A$ to $\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor].

proof_origin.place: Weibel Theorem 2.4.6 with Lemma 2.2.8; Stacks Tags 0117, 0136, 013P, 013T. Lean proof follows the six steps, using Mathlib splittingOfInjective, Splitting.map, homology_exact1/2/3, delta_naturality, rightDerived_map_eq and mono_homologyMap_of_mono_of_not_rel. Additivity uses the proved upstream instance in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.RightDerived, avoiding both a duplicate proof and the degree-zero left-exact comparison.

lean.statement: theorem exists_horseshoe_rightDerived_deltaFunctor {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] [EnoughInjectives A] [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B] (v : A ⥤ B) [v.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits v] : ∃ (G : CohomologicalDeltaFunctor A B) (hF : G.F = (fun n : ℕ ↦ v.rightDerived n)), ∀ (S : ShortComplex A) (hS : S.ShortExact) (IA : InjectiveResolution S.X₁) (IB : InjectiveResolution S.X₂) (IC : InjectiveResolution S.X₃) (α : IA.cocomplex ⟶ IB.cocomplex) (β : IB.cocomplex ⟶ IC.cocomplex) (hαβ : α ≫ β = 0) (_hιA : IA.ι ≫ α = (CochainComplex.single₀ A).map S.f ≫ IB.ι) (_hιB : IB.ι ≫ β = (CochainComplex.single₀ A).map S.g ≫ IC.ι) (_hH : ∀ k : ℕ, ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map (HomologicalComplex.eval A (ComplexShape.up ℕ) k)).ShortExact), ∃ hvH : ((ShortComplex.mk α β hαβ).map (v.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ))).ShortExact, ∀ n : ℕ, G.delta S hS n ≫ eqToHom (congrArg (fun F ↦ (F (n + 1)).obj S.X₁) hF) = eqToHom (congrArg (fun F ↦ (F n).obj S.X₃) hF) ≫ (IC.isoRightDerivedObj v n).hom ≫ hvH.δ n (n + 1) rfl ≫ (IA.isoRightDerivedObj v (n + 1)).inv

reviewed_lean.note: A,B abelian, EnoughInjectives A, v Additive+PreservesFiniteLimits, G.F = rightDerived; every horseshoe (IA,IB,IC,α,β, complex-level augmentations, degreewise SES) gives v(H) SES and G.delta = isoRightDerivedObj-transported snake δ (iota order matches node); clause (1)/(2) via G.naturality/exactness fields; no claim vs triangle δ
